clue.text: Crow eating variety of cakes is indifferent

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of the next word take a new order
a bird eating something holds it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crow pecks at an assortment of cakes, unbothered by anything around it.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK EASY is an old Chambers phrase; the anagram of cakes sits inside JAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jack easy means not caring either way, an old colloquial term for nonchalance or unconcern.

clue.text: Stone wall (unbroken) restricted reported jail-break in charge of 7 14

indicators.note: to be restricted is to be hemmed in, so the general's name closes round the other part
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want the sound of the phrase

blocks.note: joined up as one word, Stonewall was the nickname of the Confederate general Thomas Jackson
nick is slang for jail and a hole is a break

explanation.surface: A prison wall stays intact despite rumours of an escape, while someone takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket tells you to read 'Stone wall' as the single word Stonewall. Jack Nicholson played the devil Daryl Van Horne, who presides over the three women in The Witches of Eastwick.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholson's character is the diabolical seducer who gathers and controls the coven in the film, so he is its master.

clue.text: Reporter's divvy for one of 7 14

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so we use its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a divvy is a dividend or portion, a share

explanation.surface: A journalist claims a cut of the proceeds for one of the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer and actress played Alexandra, one of the three women in the 1987 film The Witches of Eastwick.

clue.text: Dry up! Will's being a good listener

blocks.note: ens is the philosophers' Latin word for a being or entity
someone with an ear for something listens well

explanation.surface: A plea for someone to shut up, while Will is praised for listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry up!' looks like a rude interruption, but it is the definition, and 'Will's' marks it as Shakespeare's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensear is an archaic Shakespearean verb meaning to make dry or wither, used in Timon of Athens.

clue.text: One of 7 14 gets us up without a sweater to put on

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
sans is the French-derived word for without
an Aran is a thick cable-knit jumper from the Aran Islands
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: One of the stars rouses us, then goes off without a jumper to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actress played Jane, one of the three women in the film The Witches of Eastwick.

clue.text: "Upbringing?" Over-acknowledge Enigmatist, if you like

definitions.note: the answer is a thing that does the bringing up, not the act

indicators.note: turning something over puts it the other way round, so the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: to cite a source is to acknowledge it
the setter refers to himself, so his name stands for me

explanation.surface: A setter asks to be thanked too much, as though discussing a childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbringing' looks like child-rearing; read as up-bringing, it is something that makes you vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that induces vomiting, literally bringing the stomach contents up.

clue.text: One of 7 14 rodents round abyss with pair, if restricted by irons?

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the small animals surround the pit
a word restricted by others is penned in between them

blocks.note: mice are small rodents
hell is the bottomless pit or abyss
PR is the standard abbreviation for pair
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, so two irons give it twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rats circle a chasm in fetters, a nightmarish image with a film star attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, so 'irons' doubles it. 'restricted by' puts the little word between the two irons, then the pair encloses that group.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress played Sukie, one of the three women in the 1987 film The Witches of Eastwick.

clue.text: Cut into bird: revolutionary, so eat well with port and play

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so the first word goes within the bird

blocks.note: to hew is to cut with blows
a tit is a small songbird
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
taken as written
to feast is to eat lavishly
Wick is a harbour town in Caithness, northern Scotland

explanation.surface: A recipe: carve a bird, have a radical round, dine well with port, then see a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine served after dinner, but it is a Scottish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: John Updike's novel became a 1987 film and later a stage musical, so the theatre version qualifies as a stage work.

clue.text: Treats as a loss and leaves in a hurry

blocks.note: first meaning: writes off a debt or cost in the accounts
second meaning: rushes away, as if launching an attack

explanation.surface: A bankrupt trader books the loss and storms out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb serves both for writing off an expense in bookkeeping and for dashing away suddenly.

clue.text: Reacts to very witty joke and credit relaxes

blocks.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit
to ease up is to relax or slacken

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a gag while the bank loosens its lending.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease up is British slang for doubling over with laughter at something very funny.

clue.text: Romantic letters with 26p stamps to LA?

blocks.note: letters are the post, the mail
26p was the price of a first-class stamp in Britain in the 1990s, so they are class one
letters to Los Angeles are addressed to Cal, short for California

explanation.surface: Love letters, properly stamped, are sent off to Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' suggests love letters, but it is the musical period that followed the Classical era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic period in music and art came directly after the Classical era, so it is later than that style.

clue.text: Novice companion knocking back beer

indicators.note: knocking a drink back suggests sending it backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A beginner and a friend sink a pint together.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is a disciple or pupil of a guru in Hindu and Buddhist tradition, a learner starting out.

clue.text: About the flow of Ganges and Rhine, one may be issuing a legal warning

indicators.note: rivers flowing about wander and twist, so their letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone watching two great rivers flow issues a formal caution.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnishee is to serve a court notice on a third party, warning them to hold back money owed to a debtor.

clue.text: Interloper makes Parisian very cross

blocks.note: très is French for very
passer is the French verb to cross, still in Paris

explanation.surface: An intruder makes a Frenchman furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but 'Parisian' covers it too: it is the French verb to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone who intrudes on land or property without permission, an unwelcome intruder.

clue.text: See 7
Right behind Kon-tiki, say

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
aft means at the back, especially on a boat

explanation.surface: Someone is following directly behind the Kon-Tiki.
explanation.definitionFit: Kon-Tiki was Thor Heyerdahl's balsa-log vessel that crossed the Pacific in 1947, an example of a floating platform.

clue.text: Arms are as good as hair

blocks.note: something that is a match for another is as good as it
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A claim that limbs are every bit as fine as one's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' reads as limbs next to hair, but it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchlocks are early muskets fired by a slow match, so they are firearms or weapons.

clue.text: See 6
Strangely east of Java, but not very, crosses bridge in the Pacific

definitions.note: a phrase locating the answer rather than a noun for it

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so one letter is taken away
arranged strangely means put in an odd order
something that crosses over another spans it, holding it underneath

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
a span is a bridge or the arch of one

explanation.surface: Directions to an ocean location east of Java, reached by crossing a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: V comes out of the anagram fodder before the shuffle, and the jumble sits inside SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sea of Japan is a marginal sea of the western Pacific, between Japan and the Asian mainland.

clue.text: Worker following meat

blocks.note: the worker bee is the crossword's stock worker
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A labourer trails after a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is the flesh of cattle eaten as food, one kind of red meat.

clue.text: Nothing to be seen amongst the trees but a furrow

indicators.note: something seen amongst trees stands in the middle of them, so one piece is set inside the other

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: A walker finds nothing in the woods except a trench in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel cut into a surface, like a rut or furrow.

clue.text: Ford, etc, one sorting out river test

indicators.note: sorting things moves them about into a different arrangement

blocks.note: a means one, as in a single item
taken as written
the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: Someone named Ford, among others, is assessing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like a river crossing next to 'river', but it is the car company.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford and similar firms make cars, so together they form the motor-manufacturing sector.

clue.text: As the Arctic is reported to be, that is clear

indicators.note: reported speech is spoken out, so the sound of the description is wanted

blocks.note: the Arctic is freezing cold, which is icy

explanation.surface: A comment on polar weather, followed by agreement that the point is understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying I see signals that you understand, the same as saying the matter is now plain.

clue.text: A love-plant

blocks.note: taken as written
love is a score of zero in tennis, nil

explanation.surface: A love-plant sounds like a herb with romantic powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the West Indian indigo shrub, a dye-yielding plant of the pea family.

clue.text: Dead thick, I won't tip

blocks.note: first meaning: a corpse, in slang
a further meaning: dense or not flowing easily
last meaning: to refuse a waiter a gratuity, in American slang

explanation.surface: A miserly, stupid diner announces he will leave nothing for the waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really three meanings in one: a corpse, firm in consistency, and to cheat someone of a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a dead body, and to stiff a waiter means to withhold the expected gratuity.

clue.text: See 1 down
In the garden to clear lines is profligacy

blocks.note: a gardener clears leaves with a rake
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: Tidying up the garden is called wasteful extravagance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakery is the dissolute conduct of a rake, a libertine, hence debauchery or wild living.

clue.text: Reopened line in Sussex down to the signal

blocks.note: feeling down is feeling blue
a bell rings as a signal

explanation.surface: A restored railway runs down to its signal box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' and 'signal' set a railway scene, and the definition really is one: the Bluebell Railway, a preserved steam line in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bluebell Railway was closed by British Railways and reopened by volunteers in 1960 as a heritage route.
